verdict.line: You lose if you trade into his boomerang before mist is up; you win once Dusk and Dawn and Shadowflame come online and he's stuck fighting your passive's %health damage.

brief.thesis: Gnar's 1100-range Boomerang Throw and transform-stun combo are why he holds the lane and solo-kill edge, but Gwen's W (Hallowed Mist) makes her untargetable to anything outside it, which voids his poke if you play patient instead of standing in his face. That's the structural reason the head-to-head sits at 51.8% over 623 games even though the raw lane stats say Gnar.

theirWindow.when: rage bar near full, about to transform
theirWindow.what: Back off and reset. Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) stuns an area and his R (GNAR!) can slow and wall-stun you for bonus damage — don't be standing in a line to a wall when his rage caps.

yourWindow.when: Gnar just reverted from Mega form
yourWindow.what: Rage resets to empty on revert and his Q (Boulder Toss CD 16-10s) is usually spent. Use E (Skip 'n Slash) to dash in immediately for the attack speed/range window while he has no stun and no poke up.

powerCurve.note: Mist negates poke, Dusk and Dawn online

start.why: Runs at 53.8% over 533 games and is picked 70.6% of the time — the extra sustain from the potions matters more here than the shield variant because Gnar's early poke is ranged, not melee trades.

boots.why: 51.3% win rate over 234 games, beating Plated Steelcaps' 48.2%. The magic pen pushes your burst through Gnar's armor-stacking Mega form faster than the steelcaps' auto-attack mitigation pays off.

core.why: First item in the 60.3%-winrate path (146 games) — ability haste keeps your W mist and E dash resets cycling through his poke windows.
The bonus damage to low-health targets stacks with A Thousand Cuts' %health magic damage, which is specifically what punishes Mega Gnar's inflated HP bar.
Caps the 60.3%-winrate build with the AP scaling that turns your Q and R into real burst once lane is stabilized.

you need omnivamp to win extended duels instead of burst (60% WR over 15 games)
you're ahead and want attack speed to snowball through squishier mini-Gnar windows

runes.keystoneWhy: Both measured rune pages run Conqueror as keystone — the stacking adaptive force from sustained trading is how Gwen out-scales Gnar's burst poke over a fight.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport runs 52.2% over a large sample and lets you reset after bad poke exchanges or go split push, which matters since you're behind in the early trading window. Flash+Ignite (50.9%, the most popular pick at 49.3%) is the aggressive alternative if you plan to all-in off E resets; Ghost+Teleport posts the highest win rate (56.8%) but on a smaller sample and suits a sidelane-focused game plan.

playing.title: Hold W until he commits
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist only protects you from enemies outside it — if you pop it the instant he throws Boomerang Throw from max range, he just walks away and resets. Bait him to within melee range first.

playing.title: Never fight into a full rage bar
playing.detail: Once Gnar's rage bar nears max he's one ability away from Mega form's W (Wallop) stun. Disengage before that threshold instead of trading through it.

playing.title: All-in the instant he reverts
playing.detail: Transforming back to mini Gnar resets his rage to zero and usually means his Q is on cooldown (16 down to 10s by rank 5). Dash in with E (Skip 'n Slash) for the attack speed and range window right then.

playing.title: Close distance before using Q
playing.detail: Snip Snip! only reaches 450 range — you cannot out-poke a 1100-range boomerang by standing still. Use E to close the gap before committing Q charges.

playing.title: Don't let him re-catch the boomerang
playing.detail: Catching Boulder Toss cuts its cooldown, which is how he keeps poke rolling. Punish his position when the boomerang is mid-flight back to him instead of letting him walk under it safely.

playing.title: Build for his HP bar, not his armor
playing.detail: Shadowflame's execute-adjacent damage plus A Thousand Cuts' %health magic damage is what actually closes out fights against Mega Gnar's bloated health pool — prioritize that over flat damage items.

playing.title: Accept the early deficit
playing.detail: Levels 1-8 are genuinely his through poke range and transform threats. Play for CS and cooldowns, not kills, until Dusk and Dawn and Shadowflame are both up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample numbers above are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch (16.19.1). The matchup read — why the mist negates his poke, why the rage bar is the tell, why Shadowflame matters against Mega Gnar's HP — is my own tactical analysis layered on top of that data.
